Outsourced NDT Level III support in South Carolina: aerospace suppliers and industrial employers

In South Carolina, a large share of outsourced NDT Level III work comes from the aerospace supply chain around Boeing's 787 plant in North Charleston and Toray's composite materials site in Spartanburg. Industrial fabricators and inspection companies that run SNT-TC-1A programs add the rest. Atlantis, based in Houston, provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting through remote document review and scheduled site visits.

The aerospace chain. Boeing moved all 787 production to North Charleston in 2021. Before that, the plant was already the only one building the 787-10. Toray Composite Materials America supplies Boeing with intermediate-modulus, toughened carbon fiber prepreg for primary structure, and its Spartanburg site was set up to combine precursor, fiber and prepreg production in one plant. Machine shops, composite fabricators and assembly suppliers selling into that chain usually face two requirements. The first is Nadcap NDT accreditation, audited against AC7114 and method checklists such as AC7114/1 for penetrant, AC7114/3 for ultrasonic and AC7114/4 for film radiography. The second is personnel qualification to NAS 410 under a named Responsible Level 3.

What Atlantis does, and what it does not. Atlantis's ASNT NDT Level III covers UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. It writes and revises SNT-TC-1A written practices, develops and approves procedures and technique sheets, sets and grades Level I and II examinations under the employer's written practice, audits programs, and approves subcontractors. Before a Nadcap audit, it can review procedures, calibration and personnel records against the checklist the auditor will use. The NAS 410 Responsible Level 3 role is provided only through an associate. Atlantis staff do not hold NAS 410, and Atlantis is not a certification body or an accredited inspection or testing body. Those limits are stated in every proposal, so a supplier knows exactly whose name goes on which document.

Industrial employers. Outside aerospace, the typical South Carolina client is a fabricator or inspection company working to ASME Section V and VIII and AWS D1.1. It needs one dependable Level III instead of a full-time hire. The first review usually finds the same few problems. The written practice no longer matches how the crews work, vision examinations or on-the-job hours are missing from certification files, and nobody can say which procedure revision applied to a job from last year.

  • SNT-TC-1A written practice: authoring, annual review and revision control
  • Method procedures and technique sheets, including composite UT for aerospace parts
  • Level I and II examinations administered under the employer's own written practice
  • Pre-audit review against Nadcap AC7114 checklists
  • NAS 410 Level 3 duties through an associate, stated in writing
  • Certification and calibration records held in the ERP certificates app

Next steps. The full consulting scope is on outsourced NDT Level III consulting, procedure work is on NDT procedure development, and program setup is on SNT-TC-1A program setup. The aerospace-specific rules are explained on aerospace NDT consulting, and Upstate support is covered on NDT consulting in Greenville. Technician courses are on NDT training in South Carolina. To start, send your written practice and audit date through the South Carolina consulting enquiry.
